claims.subject: mathematical-optimum bell nozzle contours
claims.object: gas properties; a single canted parabola closely approximates them for a given area ratio and length
claims.statement: Bell-nozzle contours from the mathematical-optimum design method vary only slightly with gas properties; for a given area ratio and length a single canted parabola very closely approximates the variety of optimum contours for the chamber conditions that may occur in rocket engines.
claims.quote: a single canted parabola will very closely approximate the variety

claims.subject: near-optimum parabolic (canted-parabola) contours
claims.object: many engineering applications, generated without a computer using Figure 5 wall angles
claims.statement: For engineering purposes near-optimum parabolic contours are suitable for many applications and can be generated without a computer; Figure 5 shows the canted-parabola contour and the initial and final wall angles for a range of area ratios and lengths.
qualifiers: Reviewer observation of Figure 5(b) on original PDF p.29: alpha_i rises and alpha_e falls with A_e/A_t for every %L = 60-100; curves solid from about A_e/A_t 3.7 to 50 and dashed to about 100. Digitized values are reviewer measurements in the P1 comparison record, not source-stated numbers.
claims.quote: near-optimum parabolic contours are suitable for many applications

claims.subject: available nozzle-contour optimization methods
claims.object: assumptions that often only roughly approximate actual conditions
claims.statement: The available nozzle-contour optimization methods are based on assumptions that often only roughly approximate the actual conditions.
claims.quote: are based on assumptions that often only roughly
